content:
The example worker from TauCetiProject/TauCetiWorker now includes a command to estimate the costs of running the worker (assuming API pricing for inference). It reads the logs from your past workers, so it represents the cost estimates based on your local work, not of our whole collaborative effort. If you have been running lots of workers for a long time it may take a while to analyze the data!

(The output is pretty messy and disorganized, if someone would like to make this nice, and focus on the useful information that would be lovely.)

The headline is the estimate that adding the N-th line of code to TauCeti is costing very roughly $7∗10−2+$6∗10−10N \$7*10^{-2} + \$6*10^{-10} N$7∗10−2+$6∗10−10N, i.e. about 7c per LOC, with the non-linearities not dominating until about N=108N=10^8N=108 (I would take the nonlinearity estimate with a large pinch of salt). Another estimate I've done recently using only the newer models suggests closer to 3c per LOC.
So 70k per MLoC makes 210k USD, kinda seems high.

One “clear” way to optimize for cost is to use a cheaper model. But we don't know if quality suffers accordingly. Proceed with caution I guess.
#Tau Ceti > Harness improvements?

We do know AI companies are heavily subsidizing these for now, but even if they're paying for the tokens, it still consumes energy.

I guess #Autoformalization > Luna (!) only Trellis formulation of Bradač Ramsey paper can be used for comparison. That one is .23 cents per line. Given Luna is 100× cheaper than Astra, I suppose it checks out wait it doesn't check out…
